correctness.rationale: The safe marked configurations are an exact projection for the pre-deletion-complement update. At insertion parameter ε=(n−r)⁻¹=0, the empty state carries the simple eigenvalue 1 and the other eigenvalues are 1−j/r. Differentiating the left eigenvector equation at zero gives mass rε+O(ε²) on each singleton and O(ε²) in total on larger states: the perturbation from the empty state reaches only singletons, and the larger-state block has no eigenvalue 1. Killing from a singleton v occurs at rate (r−1)deg(v)ε/r, so the top eigenvalue deficit is 2(r−1)kε²+O(ε³) for any fixed graph of k forbidden pairs, including overlapping pairs. The complementary spectral powers have a uniform geometric bound by a resolvent contour strictly inside the unit circle. The stationary initial law gives leading prefactor 1+O(n⁻¹), including time-zero killing. At the claimed time, the O(n⁻³) eigenvalue error contributes O(log n/n) in the exponent; all fixed factorial moments converge to those of Poisson(e⁻ˣ). The one-pair survival bound summed beyond (1+η)aₙ log Mₙ contributes o(aₙ log Mₙ), giving the expectation with the probability lower bound. The reported 212 finite assertions concern projection and rate estimates; the uploaded checker was inspected, not executed, and no independent numerical replay is claimed.

evidence: Theorem 2.3 gives a Gumbel law for independent rounds; Theorem 2.5 proves the diagonal Markovian case r=s; Conjecture 2.4 only proposes the off-diagonal mean. The stationary mass of one pair target is r(r−1)/(2Mₙ), whereas the entrance flux is (r−1)/Mₙ.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither independence, the diagonal theorem, nor a substitution of stationary mass gives the assigned law. In contrast, the stronger indexed shadow theorem gives the exact law and mean directly.

evidence: A pair is observed exactly when it belongs to the 2-shadow of a visited r-set. The indexed shadow theorem and the assigned pair theorem both swap a uniform in-set label for a uniform label from the pre-update complement.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The shadow and super-coupon terminology does not change the target family, update rule or cover-time event. An independent-block model is not equivalent.

evidence: The shadow finding is a distinct indexed record, not the assigned record itself. The one-sided pair-cover finding, offsets 1059–1321, has the sharp upper constant and critical-scale expected missing count only.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These are theorem catalog matches rather than a finite parameter table. The shadow record covers the exact target as a specialization; the one-sided record alone does not.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed Resultary finding gives the same Gumbel law and leading expectation for every fixed subset size 1≤s<r under the same walk, with the same normalization at s=2. That is affirmative statement-level coverage of the full finding. The shared date does not establish priority. The published super-coupon paper itself does not give this strict off-diagonal Markovian result.
residual_risks: The common catalog date does not determine priority, provenance or direction of dependence.

The bounded literature check did not settle whether a separate rare-set capacity theorem also implies the law; a mass-only argument would miss the cluster factor. Neither issue negates the verified exact indexed coverage.
